# BumpCast

> BumpCast is flight tracking for nervous flyers. The iPhone app gives live flight status and delay alerts, plus a calm turbulence forecast for your exact route: when the bumps will come, how strong they'll be, and when they'll end. No ads, no account. Published by Akinyemi & Co Ltd.

BumpCast is an alternative to the top 10 flight tracking apps in the world: Flightradar24, FlightAware, Flighty, Plane Finder, FlightStats, TripIt, The Flight Tracker, Flightview, AirNav RadarBox and Planes Live. Like them, it tracks your flight's status, gates and delays. Unlike them, it is built for nervous flyers and forecasts the turbulence on your route.

- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447 ("BumpCast Flight: Turbulence", iPhone, free to download)
- Languages: English and Spanish
- Coverage: detailed forecasts for flights within the continental United States and southern Canada. Elsewhere, "Global outlooks (beta)" in Settings gives an approximate outlook for international routes, Europe included.
- Support: support@akinyemi.ca (replies usually within a day)

## Key features

### Find and track your flight
- Type a flight number (like AC 1504 or B6 23) and the day you fly, and BumpCast fills in the airports and times. Or pick your airports and choose from that day's nonstops.
- Add connecting flights in a row.
- Live status, free for every flight: delays, gate and terminal changes, cancellations and diversions.
- One gentle alert when your flight is delayed. The forecast moves with the new departure time, with one alert for both.

### Turbulence forecast for your exact route
- Turbulence is weather, and weather can be forecast. BumpCast maps the route from takeoff to landing, including climb, cruise and descent.
- A simple grade for the whole flight ("Smooth", "A few bumps", "Bumpy in places") and a calm minute-by-minute timeline.
- A plain note on each bumpy stretch: when it starts, how long it lasts, and why it happens there.
- Minutes of smooth air and of turbulence, and gusty takeoffs and landings.
- Four levels, described by how they feel: Smooth (your drink stays still), Light chop (your drink ripples), Moderate (drinks can spill; stay seated), Strong (rare; your belt keeps you safe).

### A forecast that gets sharper as you get closer
- Advance forecast 48 hours before departure.
- Updates at 24, 6 and 2 hours out, each saying what changed and why.
- "Confirmed forecast" from high-resolution data on the day you fly.
- Every forecast shows how confident it is and when it was last updated.

### In the air
- The countdown times itself to your real takeoff once it's reported, or tap "We've taken off" to set it yourself.
- Lock Screen Live Activity and Dynamic Island count down to the next bumpy stretch.
- A gentle heads-up two minutes before each stretch.
- Works in airplane mode: the forecast is saved on the phone before boarding.

### Calm, on cue
- Guided breathing paced to the next bumpy stretch.
- Short, factual explainers: what causes bumps at cruise, over mountains and near clouds, why planes are built for it, and what each level feels like.
- Calm, honest wording. No red alerts, no scare graphics.

### Turbulence map
- Turbulence across the country by altitude, now and up to 6 hours ahead, with your route drawn on top.
- Live pilot reports of what planes are actually feeling (Pro).

### After you land
- Rate how bumpy it really felt (Smoother, About right, Bumpier). Every rating is checked against the forecast, and accuracy is published in the app.

### Flights from your email (coming soon, Pro, optional)
- Connect Gmail read-only and BumpCast adds upcoming flights automatically.
- Booking emails are read on the iPhone and never reach BumpCast's servers or get stored. Only flight number, date and airports are used.

## Free and Pro

- **Free**: flight search, live status with gate changes and delay alerts, a forecast grade for up to 2 upcoming flights, and the "forecast ready" notification.
- **Pro**: every forecast update (including after delays and when confirmed), the minute-by-minute timeline, minutes of smooth air and turbulence, gusty takeoffs and landings, the in-flight Live Activity and reminders, pilot reports on the map, and unlimited flights.
- Ways to buy Pro: Flight Pass (one flight, one-time purchase), or BumpCast Pro Monthly or Annual (annual includes a 7-day free trial). Prices are shown in the App Store for your region.

## Data and privacy

- No account, no ads. This website has no cookies, analytics or third-party scripts.
- Weather data: forecasts, warnings and pilot reports from the US National Weather Service (NOAA), and modified ECMWF open data (CC BY 4.0).
- Users can ask support to delete everything linked to their device; it's done within 30 days.
- BumpCast is for comfort and planning, not for flight operations. Always follow your crew's instructions.

## Learn: turbulence explained

The app's Learn library, published at https://bumpcast.app/learn/. Short, factual explainers: why flights get bumpy, what the crew is doing, and what you'll feel, with sourced detail (FAA, NTSB, US regulations). Each link is the Markdown copy of the page (drop the .md for the web page). All of them in full: https://bumpcast.app/llms-full.txt

### Why it gets bumpy

- [Clear-air turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/learn/clear-air-turbulence.html.md): Clear-air turbulence is bumpy air at cruising height, often in clear skies, where the fast jet stream flows next to slower air. It's usually light chop.
- [Mountain waves](https://bumpcast.app/learn/mountain-wave-turbulence.html.md): Mountain waves form when strong wind blows across mountains and makes waves in the air, like water over rocks in a stream. They can reach cruising height.
- [Around clouds](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-near-clouds.html.md): Warm air rising inside and around big clouds stirs the air nearby. Bumps in puffy clouds are usually brief, and pilots fly around storms, often by many miles.
- [Near the ground](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-on-takeoff-and-landing.html.md): Close to the ground, wind flows over buildings, hills and warm land, so the lowest few thousand feet are often a bit bumpy. It usually lasts only a few minutes.
- [Gusty at the airport](https://bumpcast.app/learn/gusty-takeoffs-and-landings.html.md): On a windy day, the wind near the ground speeds up and slows down over buildings and land. You feel it for a few minutes as you climb out and on the way down.

### Good to know

- [Planes are built for it](https://bumpcast.app/learn/planes-are-built-for-turbulence.html.md): Airliners are designed and tested to handle forces well beyond anything turbulence produces in normal flight. Turbulence is a comfort issue, not a structural one.
- [Why the seatbelt matters](https://bumpcast.app/learn/why-the-seatbelt-matters.html.md): Almost all turbulence injuries happen to people who aren't buckled in. Keep your seatbelt loosely fastened whenever you're seated, even with the sign off.
- [Light, moderate, strong](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-levels.html.md): Light chop is small rhythmic bumps, moderate is noticeable jolts, and strong is hard jolts that push you against your belt. Most flights see light chop at most.
- [How BumpCast forecasts](https://bumpcast.app/learn/how-bumpcast-forecasts-turbulence.html.md): BumpCast gives an advance turbulence forecast up to two days before your flight, then confirms it about 18 hours before departure and updates it every hour until you fly.

# Learn library: every explainer in full

## Why it gets bumpy

### Clear-air turbulence

> Bumps at cruise, often in clear skies.

Clear-air turbulence is bumpy air at cruising height, often in clear skies, where the fast jet stream flows next to slower air. It's usually light chop.

#### What causes clear-air turbulence?

High up, fast rivers of wind (the jet stream) flow next to slower air. Where they meet, the air tumbles a little, like water where a fast stream meets a still pool.

#### What do pilots do about clear-air turbulence?

Pilots get forecasts and reports from planes ahead, and often climb or descend a few thousand feet to find smoother air. They turn on the seatbelt sign before it starts.

#### What does clear-air turbulence feel like?

Usually light chop: a gentle, rhythmic rocking. Your drink ripples.

#### Good to know

This is the most common kind of bump at cruise, and the plane is built for far more than it can produce.

#### In more detail

##### How fast and how high is the jet stream?

Jet streams are narrow bands of strong wind from about 20,000 to 45,000 feet, the heights where airliners cruise. They blow from west to east and can top 275 miles per hour. The speed itself isn't what makes bumps: it's the sharp change in wind speed at the jet's edges, where the air rolls over in waves.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

##### When is clear-air turbulence most common?

In winter. Jet streams follow the boundary between warm and cold air, which is sharpest in winter, so that's when they're strongest. Over the US, clear-air turbulence is found most often on the north side of the jet stream, near the top of the lower atmosphere (the tropopause).

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

##### How big is a patch of clear-air turbulence?

Patches near the jet stream are typically 100 to 300 miles long, 50 to 100 miles wide and about 5,000 feet deep, and they can last from half an hour to a day. That's why a climb or descent of a few thousand feet often finds smoother air, and why reports from planes ahead help so much.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

##### Is it bumpier at cruise in winter?

In pilot reports, yes. In BumpCast's analysis of 320,865 airliner reports at cruising height over the US and southern Canada (November 2025 to October 2026), moderate or stronger bumps made up about 1.3 times as large a share of reports from December to February as from June to August.

Source: [Turbulence by route: a year of pilot reports and airport weather](https://bumpcast.app/routes/)

#### More turbulence types

- [Mountain waves](https://bumpcast.app/learn/mountain-wave-turbulence.html.md): Wind rolling over high ground
- [Around clouds](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-near-clouds.html.md): Rising air near big clouds
- [Near the ground](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-on-takeoff-and-landing.html.md): Climbing and descending

Source: https://bumpcast.app/learn/clear-air-turbulence.html (updated 2026-11-07). From the Learn library in BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

### Mountain waves

> Wind rolling over high ground.

Mountain waves form when strong wind blows across mountains and makes waves in the air, like water over rocks in a stream. They can reach cruising height.

#### What causes mountain wave turbulence?

Strong wind blowing across mountains makes waves in the air, much like water flowing over rocks in a stream. They can reach cruising height.

#### How do pilots handle mountain waves?

Crews know where mountain waves are likely and plan altitudes around them. They slow to a calmer speed if needed.

#### What do mountain waves feel like?

A slow rise and fall, sometimes with light chop.

#### Good to know

The bumps follow the terrain, so they usually pass once you're beyond the mountains.

#### In more detail

##### How much wind does it take to make mountain waves?

Not much. Wind of 15 knots or more blowing across a range at an angle of at least 30 degrees can set them off, and the waves can roll on for many miles downwind. Satellite pictures of the Rockies have shown them stretching 700 miles.

Source: [Aeronautical Information Manual, 7-6-7: Mountain Flying](https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap7_section_6.html)

##### How high do mountain waves reach?

Some waves travel upward and can be felt far above the peaks, at times above 60,000 feet. Where they break, the bumps are usually between about 20,000 and 39,000 feet, which is where jets cruise as they cross the range.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

##### Can you see mountain waves?

Sometimes. Smooth, lens-shaped clouds (lenticular clouds) over and downwind of mountains show the waves are there. Smooth edges go with little or no turbulence; lumpy, rolling ones with more. In dry air the waves can be there with no clouds at all. The strongest mountain winds usually come from late autumn to early spring.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

#### More turbulence types

- [Clear-air turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/learn/clear-air-turbulence.html.md): Bumps at cruise, often in clear skies
- [Near the ground](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-on-takeoff-and-landing.html.md): Climbing and descending

Source: https://bumpcast.app/learn/mountain-wave-turbulence.html (updated 2026-11-07). From the Learn library in BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

### Around clouds

> Rising air near big clouds.

Warm air rising inside and around big clouds stirs the air nearby. Bumps in puffy clouds are usually brief, and pilots fly around storms, often by many miles.

#### Why is it bumpy around clouds?

Warm air rising inside and around big clouds stirs the air nearby.

#### How do pilots avoid storms?

Pilots see storms on radar and fly around them, often by many miles. That's why your route might curve.

#### What does turbulence near clouds feel like?

Short bumps as you pass through puffy clouds; usually brief.

#### Good to know

Avoiding storms is routine; air traffic control expects planes to route around them.

#### In more detail

##### How far do pilots stay from thunderstorms?

The FAA tells pilots to stay at least 20 miles from any thunderstorm that's severe or shows up strongly on radar. The rising and sinking air reaches well beyond the cloud: severe turbulence can be found up to 20 miles from a severe storm, and about 10 miles from weaker ones. That margin is why your route might bend around a line of storms.

Source: [Aeronautical Information Manual, chapter 7, section 1: Meteorology](https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap7_section_1.html)

##### Why is it smooth above the clouds?

Puffy, cauliflower-shaped cumulus clouds mark rising air, and their tops show roughly where it stops rising. So it's often bumpy beneath and in them, and generally smooth above. They grow on sunny afternoons over land, which is one reason a summer afternoon climb or descent can feel bumpier than the cruise.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

#### More turbulence types

- [Clear-air turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/learn/clear-air-turbulence.html.md): Bumps at cruise, often in clear skies
- [Near the ground](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-on-takeoff-and-landing.html.md): Climbing and descending

Source: https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-near-clouds.html (updated 2026-11-07). From the Learn library in BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

### Near the ground

> Climbing and descending.

Close to the ground, wind flows over buildings, hills and warm land, so the lowest few thousand feet are often a bit bumpy. It usually lasts only a few minutes.

#### Why is it bumpy after takeoff and before landing?

Close to the ground, wind flows over buildings, hills and warm patches of land, so the lowest few thousand feet are often a bit bumpy.

#### What do pilots do near the ground?

Takeoff and landing are planned with wind in mind. Pilots keep the seatbelt sign on until the air settles.

#### What do bumps near the ground feel like?

Small bumps during the climb or the final descent, which ease as you go higher or touch down.

#### Good to know

This is normal on many flights and usually lasts only a few minutes.

#### In more detail

##### What makes the air bumpy near the ground?

Two things, mostly. Wind tumbling over trees, buildings and hills breaks into eddies; the stronger the wind and the rougher the ground, the bumpier it gets. And on sunny days, ground that heats unevenly (fields, rock, pavement, water) sends up bubbles of warm air.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

##### When is it bumpiest on the way up or down?

Rising warm air is strongest on warm summer afternoons with light wind, so in summer the climb and descent are often calmer in the morning. On windy days, at any time of year, the wind stirs up the lowest few thousand feet instead.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

##### Does the size of the plane matter?

Yes. The FAA notes that the effect of turbulence depends on the size of the aircraft, and the US turbulence forecast is made separately for light, medium and heavy aircraft.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

#### More turbulence types

- [Gusty at the airport](https://bumpcast.app/learn/gusty-takeoffs-and-landings.html.md): Windy days near the ground
- [Clear-air turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/learn/clear-air-turbulence.html.md): Bumps at cruise, often in clear skies
- [Around clouds](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-near-clouds.html.md): Rising air near big clouds

Source: https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-on-takeoff-and-landing.html (updated 2026-11-07). From the Learn library in BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

### Gusty at the airport

> Windy days near the ground.

On a windy day, the wind near the ground speeds up and slows down over buildings and land. You feel it for a few minutes as you climb out and on the way down.

#### Why are takeoffs and landings bumpy on windy days?

On a windy day, the wind near the ground speeds up and slows down as it flows over buildings and land, a bit like a river over stones. You feel it for a few minutes as you climb out and on the way down.

#### What do pilots do in gusty wind?

Pilots plan every takeoff and landing around the wind. In gusty air they fly the approach a little faster for extra control, and keep the seatbelt sign on until the air settles.

#### What does a gusty takeoff or landing feel like?

Bumps and some side-to-side sway, now and then a firmer one, that ease as you climb or once you touch down.

#### Good to know

Gusty takeoffs and landings happen every day at busy airports. Some airports don't have a wind forecast, or not until a few hours before. Your forecast still covers the climb and descent either way.

#### In more detail

##### How are gusts reported at airports?

In an airport's weather report (a METAR), a G after the wind speed gives the gusts: 22015G25KT means wind from 220 degrees at 15 knots, gusting to 25 knots. BumpCast calls an end of your flight gusty when the airport's forecast has gusts of 25 knots or more.

Source: [Aeronautical Information Manual, chapter 7, section 1: Meteorology](https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap7_section_1.html)

##### Why do pilots fly a little faster in gusty wind?

Extra speed gives extra control when the wind keeps changing. A common technique taught to pilots is to add half the gust factor to the normal approach speed: with gusts 15 knots above the steady wind, about 7 knots more. Airline crews follow their aircraft maker's and airline's own procedures, which also add a little speed in gusty air.

Source: [Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C), chapter 9: Approaches and Landings](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/airplane_handbook/10_afh_ch9.pdf)

##### Which airports have the most gusty days?

Of the 22 airports on BumpCast's route pages, the ones with the most days with gusts of 25 knots or more in November 2025 to October 2026 were JFK (157 days), DEN (155 days) and BOS (148 days). The fewest were LAX (17 days), YVR (32 days) and SEA (48 days).

Source: [Turbulence by route: a year of pilot reports and airport weather](https://bumpcast.app/routes/)

#### More turbulence types

- [Near the ground](https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-on-takeoff-and-landing.html.md): Climbing and descending
- [Clear-air turbulence](https://bumpcast.app/learn/clear-air-turbulence.html.md): Bumps at cruise, often in clear skies
- [Planes are built for it](https://bumpcast.app/learn/planes-are-built-for-turbulence.html.md): Why turbulence is a comfort issue

Source: https://bumpcast.app/learn/gusty-takeoffs-and-landings.html (updated 2026-11-07). From the Learn library in BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

## Good to know

### Planes are built for it

> Why turbulence is a comfort issue.

Airliners are designed and tested to handle forces well beyond anything turbulence produces in normal flight. Turbulence is a comfort issue, not a structural one.

#### Are planes built to handle turbulence?

Airliners are designed and tested to handle forces well beyond anything turbulence produces in normal flight. Wings flex on purpose; that's why you may see them move.

#### What do pilots do when it gets bumpy?

In bumps, pilots slow to a speed that gives the aircraft extra margin and keep flying normally.

#### Why do the drops feel so big?

Movement can feel big, but most drops are a change in height of only a few meters.

#### Good to know

Turbulence is a comfort issue, not a structural one.

#### In more detail

##### How strong are airliners built to be?

US rules for airliners (14 CFR Part 25) set the loads a plane must carry. It must handle at least 2.5 g, two and a half times its weight pressing on the wings, without lasting damage. Then a safety factor of 1.5 goes on top: the structure must hold 1.5 times those loads without breaking. That's 2.5 × 1.5, or 3.75 g.

Source: [14 CFR 25.337: Limit maneuvering load factors](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-25.337); [14 CFR 25.303: Factor of safety](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-25.303); [14 CFR 25.305: Strength and deformation](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-25.305)

##### Are planes designed for gusts and turbulence too?

Yes. The same rules require designers to work out the loads from sudden up, down and sideways gusts, and from continuous turbulence, and to build for them. At sea level the design gust is a sudden 56 feet per second (about 38 mph) of moving air.

Source: [14 CFR 25.341: Gust and turbulence loads](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/section-25.341)

Source: https://bumpcast.app/learn/planes-are-built-for-turbulence.html (updated 2026-11-07). From the Learn library in BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

### Why the seatbelt matters

> The one thing that keeps you safe.

Almost all turbulence injuries happen to people who aren't buckled in. Keep your seatbelt loosely fastened whenever you're seated, even with the sign off.

#### Who gets hurt in turbulence?

Almost all turbulence injuries happen to people who aren't buckled in, usually while standing or walking.

#### Why do flight attendants sit down?

When flight attendants sit down, it's routine caution, not an emergency.

#### What does turbulence feel like with your belt on?

With your belt on, even strong bumps are just uncomfortable.

#### Good to know

Keep it loosely fastened whenever you're seated, even with the sign off.

#### In more detail

##### How often are people hurt by turbulence?

Serious injuries are rare. The FAA's count of serious turbulence injuries on US airline flights from 2009 through 2024 lists 40 passengers and 166 crew members: about 2 or 3 passengers a year.

Source: [Turbulence: Staying Safe](https://www.faa.gov/travelers/fly_safe/turbulence)

##### Why are flight attendants hurt more often than passengers?

They're the ones up and moving when it gets bumpy. The NTSB found that from 2009 to 2018, flight attendants were 79% of the people seriously injured in turbulence on US airlines. About half of those accidents happened during descent or approach, and 60% below 20,000 feet.

Source: [Preventing Turbulence-Related Injuries in Air Carrier Operations (NTSB/SS-21/01), 2021](https://www.ntsb.gov/safety/safety-studies/Documents/SS2101.pdf)

##### Does the seatbelt really make a difference?

Yes. Of the 123 passengers and flight attendants seriously injured in those accidents, only one passenger was recorded as wearing a seatbelt at the time. The NTSB found that being seated with your belt fastened is the most effective way to avoid a turbulence injury. On US flights, passengers must keep it fastened while the seatbelt sign is on.

Source: [Preventing Turbulence-Related Injuries in Air Carrier Operations (NTSB/SS-21/01), 2021](https://www.ntsb.gov/safety/safety-studies/Documents/SS2101.pdf); [14 CFR 121.317: Passenger information requirements and seat belt requirements](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-G/part-121/subpart-K/section-121.317)

Source: https://bumpcast.app/learn/why-the-seatbelt-matters.html (updated 2026-11-07). From the Learn library in BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

### Light, moderate, strong

> What each one feels like.

Light chop is small rhythmic bumps, moderate is noticeable jolts, and strong is hard jolts that push you against your belt. Most flights see light chop at most.

#### What are the levels of turbulence?

Light chop is small rhythmic bumps. Moderate is noticeable jolts. Strong is hard jolts that push you against your belt.

#### How do pilots handle moderate and strong turbulence?

Pilots work to avoid moderate and strong bumps, changing altitude or route when they can.

#### What does each level feel like?

Light: your drink ripples. Moderate: walking is tricky and drinks can spill. Strong: rare, and your belt keeps you safe.

#### Good to know

Most flights see light chop at most.

#### In more detail

##### How does the FAA describe each level?

By what happens in the cabin. Light: you may feel a slight strain against your seatbelt, loose things may shift a little, and food service and walking carry on. Moderate: a definite strain against the belt, loose things are dislodged, and food service and walking are difficult. Severe: you're forced hard against the belt, loose things are tossed about, and walking is impossible.

Source: [Aeronautical Information Manual, chapter 7, section 1: Meteorology](https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap7_section_1.html)

##### What's the difference between light chop and light turbulence?

Pilots report two kinds of light bumps. Light chop is slight, quick, rhythmic bumpiness without noticeable changes in height or attitude: the gentle rocking most people notice at cruise. Light turbulence is slight, uneven changes in height or attitude.

Source: [Aeronautical Information Manual, chapter 7, section 1: Meteorology](https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap7_section_1.html)

##### How do forecasters measure turbulence?

With eddy dissipation rate (EDR), the international standard for automated turbulence reports. It measures the air itself, not how one plane responds, so it works for any aircraft. BumpCast's levels are set on the EDR scale.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

Source: https://bumpcast.app/learn/turbulence-levels.html (updated 2026-11-07). From the Learn library in BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

### How BumpCast forecasts

> Advance, then confirmed.

BumpCast gives an advance turbulence forecast up to two days before your flight, then confirms it about 18 hours before departure and updates it every hour until you fly.

#### How does BumpCast forecast turbulence?

Up to two days before your flight, you get an advance forecast. It can still change. About 18 hours before departure it's confirmed with a more detailed forecast along your likely route and altitude, then updated every hour until you fly.

#### Does the crew have its own forecast?

Your crew has their own forecasts and live reports, and adjusts on the day.

#### How exact is the forecast?

We assume a direct route and a typical climb, cruise and descent, so treat it as a guide, not a guarantee.

#### Good to know

We'll notify you when your forecast is confirmed and if anything changes.

#### In more detail

##### Where does BumpCast's forecast come from?

From about 18 hours before departure, the US National Weather Service's Graphical Turbulence Guidance (GTG): an automated forecast, made every hour, out to 18 hours ahead and from 1,000 to 45,000 feet. Before that, the advance forecast is BumpCast's own, from the winds in two global weather models (NOAA's GFS and ECMWF's), and on its own it never calls anything stronger than light that far out.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

##### What can't a turbulence forecast see?

Mostly the bumps in and around thunderstorms. The national forecast covers clear-air and mountain-wave turbulence but doesn't specifically predict turbulence from storms or small local terrain. So BumpCast also raises your forecast wherever an official turbulence warning (a SIGMET) or a recent pilot report covers your route, and pilots steer around storms on the day.

Source: [Aviation Weather Handbook (FAA-H-8083-28B), 2026](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/FAA-H-8083-28B.pdf)

Source: https://bumpcast.app/learn/how-bumpcast-forecasts-turbulence.html (updated 2026-11-07). From the Learn library in BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

# Turbulence by route: every route in full

## JFK to LAX turbulence

> New York (JFK) ⇄ Los Angeles (LAX), both directions. November 2025 to October 2026.

Flights between New York (JFK) and Los Angeles (LAX) fly about 2,470 miles, roughly 5 hours in the air. In the past year, pilots near this route reported moderate bumps most often over Colorado. Severe reports were rare: 120 of 35,528.

- Distance: 2,470 miles (3,970 km)
- In the air: about 5 h 5 min (typical jet, still air)
- Pilot reports near the route: 35,528
- Severe reports: 120 (0.3%)
- Gusty days: JFK 157, LAX 17

### Where on the route it gets bumpy

Moderate bumps were reported most often over Colorado, near Colorado Springs, about 3 h 20 min after leaving JFK (1 h 40 min after leaving LAX): 1,072 of 2,964 reports there. The ground below is high, and wind over mountains makes waves that reach cruising height.

The next most were over Pennsylvania, near Pittsburgh, about 40 min after leaving JFK (4 h 20 min after leaving LAX): 1,056 of 1,571 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms.

### Takeoff and landing

JFK had gusts of 25 knots or more on 157 days in the past year, most often in December (20 days). LAX had gusts of 25 knots or more on 17 days in the past year, most often in February (5 days).

### Questions

#### Is JFK to LAX a bumpy flight?

Most flights see light chop at most. From November 2025 to October 2026, pilots near the JFK–LAX route filed 35,528 turbulence reports, and severe reports were rare: 120 of 35,528 (0.3%). Pilots report bumpy air more readily than smooth, so the share of flights with strong bumps is lower still. On the day, the weather decides: BumpCast forecasts your exact flight from 48 hours before departure.

#### Where is it bumpiest between JFK and LAX?

Moderate bumps were reported most often over Colorado, near Colorado Springs, about 3 h 20 min after leaving JFK (1 h 40 min after leaving LAX): 1,072 of 2,964 reports there. The ground below is high, and wind over mountains makes waves that reach cruising height. The next most were over Pennsylvania, near Pittsburgh, about 40 min after leaving JFK (4 h 20 min after leaving LAX): 1,056 of 1,571 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms.

#### When is the smoothest time of year to fly JFK to LAX?

Moderate bumps made up a similar share of reports all year. Any month can have a smooth or a bumpy day, so the forecast for your flight matters more.

#### Is LAX to JFK the same?

Yes. It's the same air, so bumps are reported in the same places, just at different times into the flight. Flights from LAX to JFK usually take less time than the way back, with the prevailing westerly winds behind them.

#### Are takeoffs and landings bumpy at JFK and LAX?

On windy days they can be, for a few minutes. JFK had gusts of 25 knots or more on 157 days in the past year, most often in December (20 days). LAX had gusts of 25 knots or more on 17 days in the past year, most often in February (5 days).

#### Can I get a turbulence forecast for my JFK to LAX flight?

Yes. BumpCast forecasts the turbulence on your exact JFK–LAX flight from 48 hours before departure: when the bumps will come, how strong they'll be and when they'll end, and whether takeoff and landing look gusty. It's free to download on the App Store for iPhone.

### How this page was made

- Period: November 2025 to October 2026. Pilot reports (PIREPs) and airport weather reports (METARs) from the US National Weather Service, via the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/gis/pireps.php
- Reports from airliners within 60 nautical miles of the direct path, near the height a flight would be there (BumpCast's flight model). Each report counts at the strongest turbulence it names; "moderate to severe" counts as severe.
- Gusty days: days with at least one hourly report of gusts of 25 knots or more.
- Reporting habits differ: smooth air made up 4% of cruise reports at Washington Center but 45% at Miami Center. These numbers show where and when bumps were reported, compared within a route. They aren't the odds for a given flight, and routes aren't ranked against each other.

Source: https://bumpcast.app/routes/jfk-to-lax-turbulence.html (data November 2025 to October 2026). From BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447

> New York (JFK) ⇄ San Francisco (SFO), both directions. November 2025 to October 2026.

### Takeoff and landing

JFK had gusts of 25 knots or more on 157 days in the past year, most often in December (20 days). SFO had gusts of 25 knots or more on 144 days in the past year, most often in July (24 days).

### Questions

#### Is JFK to SFO a bumpy flight?

Most flights see light chop at most. From November 2025 to October 2026, pilots near the JFK–SFO route filed 32,267 turbulence reports, and severe reports were rare: 114 of 32,267 (0.4%). Pilots report bumpy air more readily than smooth, so the share of flights with strong bumps is lower still. On the day, the weather decides: BumpCast forecasts your exact flight from 48 hours before departure.

#### Where is it bumpiest between JFK and SFO?

Moderate bumps were reported most often near Cleveland, about 1 h after leaving JFK (4 h 15 min after leaving SFO): 1,110 of 1,515 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms. The next most were near JFK, where flights climb out or come in to land, about 10 min after leaving JFK (5 h 5 min after leaving SFO): 793 of 1,849 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms.

#### When is the smoothest time of year to fly JFK to SFO?

Moderate bumps made up a similar share of reports all year. Any month can have a smooth or a bumpy day, so the forecast for your flight matters more.

#### Is SFO to JFK the same?

Yes. It's the same air, so bumps are reported in the same places, just at different times into the flight. Flights from SFO to JFK usually take less time than the way back, with the prevailing westerly winds behind them.

#### Are takeoffs and landings bumpy at JFK and SFO?

On windy days they can be, for a few minutes. JFK had gusts of 25 knots or more on 157 days in the past year, most often in December (20 days). SFO had gusts of 25 knots or more on 144 days in the past year, most often in July (24 days).

Yes. BumpCast forecasts the turbulence on your exact JFK–SFO flight from 48 hours before departure: when the bumps will come, how strong they'll be and when they'll end, and whether takeoff and landing look gusty. It's free to download on the App Store for iPhone.

### Questions

#### Is LGA to ORD a bumpy flight?

Most flights see light chop at most. From November 2025 to October 2026, pilots near the LGA–ORD route filed 11,961 turbulence reports, and severe reports were rare: 79 of 11,961 (0.7%). Pilots report bumpy air more readily than smooth, so the share of flights with strong bumps is lower still. On the day, the weather decides: BumpCast forecasts your exact flight from 48 hours before departure.

#### Where is it bumpiest between LGA and ORD?

Moderate bumps were reported most often over Pennsylvania, near Pittsburgh, about 45 min after leaving LGA (55 min after leaving ORD): 451 of 643 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms. The next most were over Michigan, near Grand Rapids, about 1 h 20 min after leaving LGA (20 min after leaving ORD): 437 of 2,036 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms.

#### When is the smoothest time of year to fly LGA to ORD?

In the past year, moderate bumps made up a smaller share of reports in September and a bigger share in April. Any month can have a smooth or a bumpy day, so the forecast for your flight matters more.

#### Is ORD to LGA the same?

Yes. It's the same air, so bumps are reported in the same places, just at different times into the flight. Flights from ORD to LGA usually take less time than the way back, with the prevailing westerly winds behind them.

#### Are takeoffs and landings bumpy at LGA and ORD?

On windy days they can be, for a few minutes. LGA had gusts of 25 knots or more on 146 days in the past year, most often in December (20 days). ORD had gusts of 25 knots or more on 123 days in the past year, most often in April (20 days).

Yes. BumpCast forecasts the turbulence on your exact LGA–ORD flight from 48 hours before departure: when the bumps will come, how strong they'll be and when they'll end, and whether takeoff and landing look gusty. It's free to download on the App Store for iPhone.

Most flights see light chop at most. From November 2025 to October 2026, pilots near the BOS–DCA route filed 6,451 turbulence reports, and severe reports were rare: 55 of 6,451 (0.9%). Pilots report bumpy air more readily than smooth, so the share of flights with strong bumps is lower still. On the day, the weather decides: BumpCast forecasts your exact flight from 48 hours before departure.

#### Where is it bumpiest between BOS and DCA?

Moderate bumps were reported most often near New York, about 25 min after leaving BOS (35 min after leaving DCA): 230 of 988 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms. The next most were over Connecticut, near Hartford, about 15 min after leaving BOS (50 min after leaving DCA): 172 of 548 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms.

#### When is the smoothest time of year to fly BOS to DCA?

In the past year, moderate bumps made up a smaller share of reports in May and a bigger share in December and October. Any month can have a smooth or a bumpy day, so the forecast for your flight matters more.

#### Is DCA to BOS the same?

Yes. It's the same air, so bumps are reported in the same places, just at different times into the flight.

#### Are takeoffs and landings bumpy at BOS and DCA?

On windy days they can be, for a few minutes. BOS had gusts of 25 knots or more on 148 days in the past year, most often in December (23 days). DCA had gusts of 25 knots or more on 99 days in the past year, most often in March (14 days).

Yes. BumpCast forecasts the turbulence on your exact BOS–DCA flight from 48 hours before departure: when the bumps will come, how strong they'll be and when they'll end, and whether takeoff and landing look gusty. It's free to download on the App Store for iPhone.

### Questions

#### Is DEN to LAX a bumpy flight?

Most flights see light chop at most. From November 2025 to October 2026, pilots near the DEN–LAX route filed 14,934 turbulence reports, and severe reports were rare: 115 of 14,934 (0.8%). Pilots report bumpy air more readily than smooth, so the share of flights with strong bumps is lower still. On the day, the weather decides: BumpCast forecasts your exact flight from 48 hours before departure.

#### Where is it bumpiest between DEN and LAX?

Moderate bumps were reported most often near DEN, where flights climb out or come in to land, about 5 min after leaving DEN (1 h 50 min after leaving LAX): 1,686 of 5,113 reports there. Close to the ground, wind over the mountains stirs the air, and gusty days at DEN add to it.

#### When is the smoothest time of year to fly DEN to LAX?

In the past year, moderate bumps made up a smaller share of reports in July, August and September and a bigger share in December and June. Any month can have a smooth or a bumpy day, so the forecast for your flight matters more.

#### Is LAX to DEN the same?

Yes. It's the same air, so bumps are reported in the same places, just at different times into the flight. Flights from LAX to DEN usually take less time than the way back, with the prevailing westerly winds behind them.

#### Are takeoffs and landings bumpy at DEN and LAX?

On windy days they can be, for a few minutes. DEN had gusts of 25 knots or more on 155 days in the past year, most often in June (22 days). LAX had gusts of 25 knots or more on 17 days in the past year, most often in February (5 days).

## SEA to SFO turbulence

> Seattle (SEA) ⇄ San Francisco (SFO), both directions. November 2025 to October 2026.

Flights between Seattle (SEA) and San Francisco (SFO) fly about 680 miles, roughly 1½ hours in the air. In the past year, pilots near this route reported moderate bumps most often near SEA, and more often in November and December. Severe reports were rare: 4 of 2,463.

- In the air: about 1 h 35 min (typical jet, still air)
- Pilot reports near the route: 2,463
- Severe reports: 4 (0.2%)

### Where on the route it gets bumpy

Moderate bumps were reported most often near SEA, where flights climb out or come in to land, about 5 min after leaving SEA (1 h 30 min after leaving SFO): 152 of 506 reports there. Close to the ground, wind over buildings and land stirs the air.

The next most were over Oregon, near Portland, about 30 min after leaving SEA (1 h after leaving SFO): 107 of 200 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms.

> Dallas-Fort Worth (DFW) ⇄ Los Angeles (LAX), both directions. November 2025 to October 2026.

### Where on the route it gets bumpy

The next most were over Texas, about 45 min after leaving DFW (1 h 50 min after leaving LAX): 217 of 633 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms.

### Questions

#### Is DFW to LAX a bumpy flight?

Most flights see light chop at most. From November 2025 to October 2026, pilots near the DFW–LAX route filed 8,044 turbulence reports, and severe reports were rare: 54 of 8,044 (0.7%). Pilots report bumpy air more readily than smooth, so the share of flights with strong bumps is lower still. On the day, the weather decides: BumpCast forecasts your exact flight from 48 hours before departure.

#### Where is it bumpiest between DFW and LAX?

Moderate bumps were reported most often near DFW, where flights climb out or come in to land, about 5 min after leaving DFW (2 h 30 min after leaving LAX): 314 of 1,038 reports there. #### Is LAX to DFW the same?

Yes. It's the same air, so bumps are reported in the same places, just at different times into the flight. Flights from LAX to DFW usually take less time than the way back, with the prevailing westerly winds behind them.

#### Are takeoffs and landings bumpy at DFW and LAX?

On windy days they can be, for a few minutes. DFW had gusts of 25 knots or more on 122 days in the past year, most often in March (21 days). LAX had gusts of 25 knots or more on 17 days in the past year, most often in February (5 days).

### Takeoff and landing

DEN had gusts of 25 knots or more on 155 days in the past year, most often in June (22 days). SEA had gusts of 25 knots or more on 48 days in the past year, most often in December (18 days).

### Questions

#### Is DEN to SEA a bumpy flight?

Most flights see light chop at most. From November 2025 to October 2026, pilots near the DEN–SEA route filed 11,594 turbulence reports, and severe reports were rare: 83 of 11,594 (0.7%). Pilots report bumpy air more readily than smooth, so the share of flights with strong bumps is lower still. On the day, the weather decides: BumpCast forecasts your exact flight from 48 hours before departure.

#### Where is it bumpiest between DEN and SEA?

Moderate bumps were reported most often near DEN, where flights climb out or come in to land, about 5 min after leaving DEN (2 h 10 min after leaving SEA): 1,388 of 4,792 reports there. Close to the ground, wind over the mountains stirs the air, and gusty days at DEN add to it.

#### When is the smoothest time of year to fly DEN to SEA?

In the past year, moderate bumps made up a smaller share of reports in July and October and a bigger share in December. Any month can have a smooth or a bumpy day, so the forecast for your flight matters more.

#### Is SEA to DEN the same?

Yes. It's the same air, so bumps are reported in the same places, just at different times into the flight. Flights from SEA to DEN usually take less time than the way back, with the prevailing westerly winds behind them.

#### Are takeoffs and landings bumpy at DEN and SEA?

On windy days they can be, for a few minutes. DEN had gusts of 25 knots or more on 155 days in the past year, most often in June (22 days). SEA had gusts of 25 knots or more on 48 days in the past year, most often in December (18 days).

#### Can I get a turbulence forecast for my DEN to SEA flight?

Yes. BumpCast forecasts the turbulence on your exact DEN–SEA flight from 48 hours before departure: when the bumps will come, how strong they'll be and when they'll end, and whether takeoff and landing look gusty. It's free to download on the App Store for iPhone.

- Period: November 2025 to October 2026. Pilot reports (PIREPs) and airport weather reports (METARs) from the US National Weather Service, via the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/gis/pireps.php

### Takeoff and landing

BOS had gusts of 25 knots or more on 148 days in the past year, most often in December (23 days). ORD had gusts of 25 knots or more on 123 days in the past year, most often in April (20 days).

### Questions

#### Is BOS to ORD a bumpy flight?

Most flights see light chop at most. From November 2025 to October 2026, pilots near the BOS–ORD route filed 16,938 turbulence reports, and severe reports were rare: 63 of 16,938 (0.4%). Pilots report bumpy air more readily than smooth, so the share of flights with strong bumps is lower still. On the day, the weather decides: BumpCast forecasts your exact flight from 48 hours before departure.

#### Where is it bumpiest between BOS and ORD?

Moderate bumps were reported most often over New York, near Syracuse, about 40 min after leaving BOS (1 h 15 min after leaving ORD): 490 of 1,601 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms. The next most were over Michigan, near Detroit, about 1 h 20 min after leaving BOS (35 min after leaving ORD): 423 of 712 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms.

#### When is the smoothest time of year to fly BOS to ORD?

Moderate bumps made up a similar share of reports all year. Any month can have a smooth or a bumpy day, so the forecast for your flight matters more.

#### Is ORD to BOS the same?

Yes. It's the same air, so bumps are reported in the same places, just at different times into the flight. Flights from ORD to BOS usually take less time than the way back, with the prevailing westerly winds behind them.

#### Are takeoffs and landings bumpy at BOS and ORD?

On windy days they can be, for a few minutes. BOS had gusts of 25 knots or more on 148 days in the past year, most often in December (23 days). ORD had gusts of 25 knots or more on 123 days in the past year, most often in April (20 days).

#### Can I get a turbulence forecast for my BOS to ORD flight?

Yes. BumpCast forecasts the turbulence on your exact BOS–ORD flight from 48 hours before departure: when the bumps will come, how strong they'll be and when they'll end, and whether takeoff and landing look gusty. It's free to download on the App Store for iPhone.

### How this page was made

- Period: November 2025 to October 2026. Pilot reports (PIREPs) and airport weather reports (METARs) from the US National Weather Service, via the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/gis/pireps.php
- Reports from airliners within 60 nautical miles of the direct path, near the height a flight would be there (BumpCast's flight model). Each report counts at the strongest turbulence it names; "moderate to severe" counts as severe.
- Gusty days: days with at least one hourly report of gusts of 25 knots or more.
- Reporting habits differ: smooth air made up 4% of cruise reports at Washington Center but 45% at Miami Center. These numbers show where and when bumps were reported, compared within a route. They aren't the odds for a given flight, and routes aren't ranked against each other.

### Takeoff and landing

LGA had gusts of 25 knots or more on 146 days in the past year, most often in December (20 days). YYZ had gusts of 25 knots or more on 120 days in the past year, most often in January (18 days).

### Questions

#### Is LGA to YYZ a bumpy flight?

Most flights see light chop at most. From November 2025 to October 2026, pilots near the LGA–YYZ route filed 4,788 turbulence reports, and severe reports were rare: 38 of 4,788 (0.8%). Pilots report bumpy air more readily than smooth, so the share of flights with strong bumps is lower still. On the day, the weather decides: BumpCast forecasts your exact flight from 48 hours before departure.

#### Where is it bumpiest between LGA and YYZ?

Moderate bumps were reported most often over New York, near Rochester, about 30 min after leaving LGA (25 min after leaving YYZ): 354 of 1,267 reports there. At cruising height, bumps usually come from clear-air turbulence near the jet stream, or from clouds and storms.

#### When is the smoothest time of year to fly LGA to YYZ?

In the past year, moderate bumps made up a smaller share of reports in February and July and a bigger share in December and October. Any month can have a smooth or a bumpy day, so the forecast for your flight matters more.

#### Is YYZ to LGA the same?

Yes. It's the same air, so bumps are reported in the same places, just at different times into the flight.

#### Are takeoffs and landings bumpy at LGA and YYZ?

On windy days they can be, for a few minutes. LGA had gusts of 25 knots or more on 146 days in the past year, most often in December (20 days). YYZ had gusts of 25 knots or more on 120 days in the past year, most often in January (18 days).

#### Can I get a turbulence forecast for my LGA to YYZ flight?

Yes. BumpCast forecasts the turbulence on your exact LGA–YYZ flight from 48 hours before departure: when the bumps will come, how strong they'll be and when they'll end, and whether takeoff and landing look gusty. It's free to download on the App Store for iPhone.

### How this page was made

- Period: November 2025 to October 2026. Pilot reports (PIREPs) and airport weather reports (METARs) from the US National Weather Service, via the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/gis/pireps.php
- Reports from airliners within 60 nautical miles of the direct path, near the height a flight would be there (BumpCast's flight model). Each report counts at the strongest turbulence it names; "moderate to severe" counts as severe.
- Gusty days: days with at least one hourly report of gusts of 25 knots or more.
- Reporting habits differ: smooth air made up 4% of cruise reports at Washington Center but 45% at Miami Center. These numbers show where and when bumps were reported, compared within a route. They aren't the odds for a given flight, and routes aren't ranked against each other.

Source: https://bumpcast.app/routes/lga-to-yyz-turbulence.html (data November 2025 to October 2026). From BumpCast, the flight tracker with turbulence forecasts for nervous flyers: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824269447
